patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Wix documents a broader use-case set; OpenCart is narrower/specialist.

Comparison thesis: General-purpose vs specialist. Choose OpenCart only if your buying job matches “GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by” rather than Wix's shape. Choose Wix only if your buying job matches “Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 (sell onlin” rather than OpenCart's shape. Workflow advantage: OpenCart leans shared coverage; Wix leans checkout-conversion, catalog-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Wix documents a broader use-case set; OpenCart is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: OpenCart is GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by secondary sources (confirm live). WooCommerce kee; Wix is Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 (sell online), Business $39, Business Elite $159 (annual tile.
- Company-size focus: OpenCart (small-business, mid-market) vs Wix (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: OpenCart-leaning — vs Wix-leaning checkout-conversion, catalog-management, website-builder-commerce.
- Researched limits: OpenCart — Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Wix — Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B.

Limitations — OpenCart: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Managed cloud floors are not first-party confirmed here — confirm live before budgeting; Wix: Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B; Plan gates for selling start at Core — Free/Light are not store plans.

Poor-fit cases: OpenCart is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0 · Wix is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B · Avoid OpenCart if you actually need Wix's motion (Website-first builder with ecommerce from Core — Light $17/mo annual, Core $29 ()

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
